headline: A strong live week for MEIC (+$1,555 after fees). Research tested 28 ideas and none passed. The one apparent winner was broken by our red team.

decisions.title: Options: test a volatility-regime gate?
decisions.detail: It sizes MEIC/MNG/FLY trades by whether recent real moves beat what the morning straddle priced. It scored **29.5/40**, the only recommendation tonight. Our own data runs opposite to the published claim, so the direction must be fixed before testing.

sections.title: Research · stocks, bonds, FX, futures, crypto

rows: +14.2%/yr vs S&P +7.6% (2000–24) with genuine alpha. Passed all five statistical tests; lost to the S&P in 2017–24.
The red team found the edge came from stale fund prices. On the tradeable ETF it is only a modest crash-cutter.
Beat SPY (+9.1% vs +7.6%) but it is just the known momentum factor. The old pass was survivorship bias.

items: Single-stock anomalies are mostly known factors. Only quality-value showed real alpha.
Stale prices manufacture edges. Illiquid assets are now judged on tradeable ETFs.
Crash protection repeats in every asset class (BTC worst drop −46% vs −83%; commodities −31% vs −76%), but beating buy-and-hold does not.
Small, uncorrelated rates/FX edges (end-of-month Treasuries, FOMC-day dollar) lift a portfolio even though they fail alone.

blocks.text: **10 new building blocks** went on the shortlist. A first portfolio of 9 of them reached a Sharpe of **1.51** at 2.5% volatility. Next combinations: Greenblatt + trend overlay, and a rates/FX sleeve.
